newsitem.title: USA: U.S. housing market gains from strong economy -- NAR.
newsitem.headline: U.S. housing market gains from strong economy -- NAR.

text.p: WASHINGTON, July 25 (Reuter ) - Near-record U.S. existing home sales are being driven by a robust U.S. economy that is creating job and income growth, National Association of Realtors (NAR) economist John Tuccillo said on Friday.

"The housing market is very stong, feeding off an incredibly strong economy and, as a result, we are close to the record pace," Tuccillo said at a news conference after the group released a report showing a 2.6 percent drop in June existing home sales to a 4.14 million annual rate.
"But because in 1996 we used up so much excess demand from previous years, we are going to fall just a little bit below (the record pace)," he said.
Tuccillo attributed no special factors, such as weather, to the June figures and said the data were "no surprise."
"In terms of anecdotal evidence, talking to realtors around the country and looking at markets around the country, this is about where we should be," he said, referring to the June figures.
Tuccillo said jobs and income growth, not falling interest rates, were currently dictating the demand for housing.

"The fundamentals of the job market and growth are so overwhelming in this case that small changes in interest rates do nothing more than to provide positive background music for the market. They are not a driving force," he said.

Regarding his interest rate outlook, Tuccillo said he expects the yield on the benchmark 30-year long bond to hold around its current level of 6.43 percent for the remainder of the year. He also expects Federal Reserve policymakers to keep monetary policy steady throughout 1997.
"I don't agree with my colleagues who feel the Fed has to move before the end of the year. I think the Fed will see no reason to move and the economy will slow down," he said.
